m.d: If you own something it belongs to you, it is yours.
If you "own up" to something, you admit you did it.
m.e: I had to own up to lying about our relationship.

m.d: If something is your own it belongs to you or is about you (often used for emphasis).
m.e: I wish I had my own home.

m.d: If you are on your own, you are by yourself, there is no body else with you. This can also mean there is no one helping you.
m.e: I was on my own in the woods.

m.d: If you owe something you need to pay or give it to someone because of something you have been given.
m.e: I owe $50 to the phone company right now.

m.d: If you owe a person, there is something you need to pay or give to that person. That is, you owe something to that person.
m.e: Thanks for the help! I really owe you for that!

m.d: If you owe a lot to someone or something, you have something to thank that person (or thing) for.
m.e: We owe as much to good luck as to our own skills.

m.d: If someone says ow, they are in pain
In music, singers say ow to show that they are feeling strong emotions.
The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.
m.e: Who is the owner of this coat that was left on a chair?

m.d: Owen is a male given name.
m.e: Owen is working on a report.

m.d: An owl is a type of bird. Usually it is a large bird, with two large eyes in front, that catches smaller animals at night and sleeps during the day.
m.e: There were three owls hooting during night.

m.d: Ownership is the condition of being an owner.
You use owing to x, y to show that x is the reason for y.
m.e: Owing to the problems, we have not been able to finish.
